lines: Did you take the island staying strangely quiet after dark as a warning, or did it only make the place worse?
What kept a bad fight near Mushroom Fields from becoming the last one?
A grindstone handles nicks. I would take my time cleaning up spores and salt spotting the scabbard.
I hope you found a mushroom overhang near the shore before exhaustion made the choices for you.
I would look once at mushrooms, stew, and mooshrooms, then check the road home again.
That makes Mushroom Fields sound like odd land where even the grass changed its mind.
Mycelium underfoot is not village dirt.
Terrain like mycelium hills surrounded by open sea sounds as if it chooses the fight for you.
Who noticed that the fight at Mushroom Fields was turning against you?
The next traveler needs a warning about assuming the quiet island needs no night watch. Leave that part out and they may not return.
Steel has limits, and your account of Mushroom Fields found several of them.
A good route home beats a good blade. There, I would choose the boat landing marked from inland.
The forge teaches patience, and it sounds like Mushroom Fields demanded plenty.
If nothing hostile came near you in Mushroom Fields, keeping the blade sheathed was the right choice.
The balance may have shifted after that hard use around Mushroom Fields.
I can see why a traveler might want a sheathed sword kept dry for the voyage, though good judgment still comes first.
Could you tell where the <shake>danger</shake> was by listening at Mushroom Fields?
{target}? Strange quiet can make a place feel too safe.
If anyone heads for Mushroom Fields, tell them. Eat only what you know and keep your boat close.
A clean blade after Mushroom Fields would worry me more than a battered one.
No edge turns zombies and skeletons in the open into an easy problem. I hope you kept that in mind.
Would a lighter weapon have served you better around Plains?
Who kept their head when steel came out at Plains?
What spare part would you add before another trip to Plains?
The first thing on my bench would be any piece affected by grass seed and mud inside the sheath.
Did silence at Plains worry you more than noise?
I can prepare steel for impact. I cannot prepare a traveler for night falling before shelter is reached.
The part about grass shifting before a distant shape appears will stay with me longer than the treasure.
That makes Plains sound like wide land with nowhere to hide after dark.
What did you bring back besides the memory of animals, villages, and exposed caves?
For that journey, I would choose a sword and shield suited to open ground and keep the rest of the load light.
{target}? Open ground shows you to everything else.
Before searching anything, I would make certain I could still find the river or torch line toward home.
Even a weaponsmith knows when shelter matters more than steel. I would look for a shallow earth shelter before dusk.
Did anything at Plains sound harmless before it attacked?
A fine weapon means little when you cannot plant your feet around wide grassland with little cover.
What would you change about your gear before seeing Plains again?
A clean blade after Plains would worry me more than a battered one.
If anyone heads for Plains, tell them. Keep moving and watch the horizon.
Grass bends before <shake>trouble</shake> arrives if you look.
Did you have trouble with pollen yellowing the grip wrap on the way home?
Would you choose reach or speed if you returned to Sunflower Plains?
The balance may have shifted after that hard use around Sunflower Plains.
A traveler who spots a dugout beyond the open flowers early may never need to draw a weapon.
Tell me how you handled zombies and skeletons after sunset. That part matters more than any treasure.
{target}? Sunny fields can still point toward <shake>trouble</shake>.
What held together longer than you expected during the trip to Sunflower Plains?
What made movement around Sunflower Plains harder than the fighting?
I would slow down around bright fields where every flower faces one way. Hurrying there sounds expensive.
When did you first notice the whole field turning dark at once?
The promise of sunflowers, animals, and nearby villages would tempt plenty of travelers into staying too long.
How did the ground at Sunflower Plains change the way you held your weapon?
Was letting the cheerful view delay a night camp the moment you nearly turned back?
A good route home beats a good blade. There, I would choose the sunflower line back toward safer ground.
Did you notice the damage at Sunflower Plains, or only after returning home?
If anyone heads for Sunflower Plains, tell them. Enjoy the flowers with a torch ready.
That makes Sunflower Plains sound like bright fields that still grow dark at night.
Sunflowers face light, not safety.
I can see why a traveler might want a plain sword kept ready after dusk, though good judgment still comes first.
What opened the safest chance to get clear of Sunflower Plains?
